task: Per real detected face, MobileGaze's continuous yaw/pitch estimate (degrees), graded on plausibility - not exact accuracy, since no ground-truth gaze angle is recoverable from a static street photo without eye-tracking equipment. A prediction passes when it falls inside a generous, explicitly-stated physiological envelope (|yaw|<=60deg, |pitch|<=60deg - a face turned or tilted further than that would not read as a roughly-forward-facing photograph in the first place, which both of these are) rather than being pinned to a specific expected angle.

tolerance.note: Deliberately loose - this is a sanity bound against a physically-absurd output (e.g. the model returning a profile-view angle for a clearly frontal face), not a claim of measured accuracy.

note: Only one real, usable source image exists anywhere in this repo's committed fixtures with clearly visible human faces - stock_streetscene_3adults.jpg. Both subjects wear sunglasses (opaque, occluding the eyes) - gaze estimation models are typically trained on visible-eye imagery, so this is a harder case than clean input and is named here rather than hidden.

faces.note: Younger man, dark jacket/red top, walking toward camera-left, head roughly level, gaze direction not independently verifiable beyond 'facing generally forward/down while walking'.
Bearded man, tan coat, walking toward camera-left, head roughly level, gaze direction not independently verifiable beyond 'facing generally forward/down while walking'.
